This row read `gap` while they read `divergence` over the identical fact, which is the whole of what was wrong with it: eleven rcl graph verbs, one receiver difference, two verdicts.

WHAT WE SHIP: `rclc_executor_get_service_names_and_types_by_node` (`nros_generated.h`), with its own ledger row `c:executor_get_service_names_and_types_by_node`. Below it, `Executor::get_service_names_and_types_by_node` (`nros-node/src/executor/spin.rs`) over the phase-381 W4 vtable slot, answered by the zenoh graph cache (`nros-rmw-zenoh/src/shim/session.rs`) and, since phase-444 W3, by Cyclone (`nros-rmw-cyclonedds/src/graph_query.cpp`).

WHY THE NAME DIFFERS, and why it is not a `rename`: rcl hangs the graph off a NODE (`rcl_get_service_names_and_types_by_node(node, ...)`) because each node owns a participant. A nano-ros image opens ONE transport session for the whole image — a session per node is RAM a 128 KiB target does not have — and the Executor owns it, so the graph is asked of the Executor. Our C convention is `nros_<receiver>_<verb>`, so the receiver is IN the name; the name follows the receiver, and the receiver is where the session is. Renaming would say OUR spelling should change, and it should not.

Note this is a C-lane fact about the RECEIVER, not about the capability: the correlator matches on the normalized name, so `rclc_executor_get_service_names_and_types_by_node` can never meet `rcl_get_service_names_and_types_by_node` however the capability is spelled underneath. C++ and Rust close the same subject by FORWARDING, because those languages have a real receiver to hang the upstream name on (`cpp:Node::*`, phase-417 stage 2b; `rust:Node::*`, phase-444). C has no such move that keeps the convention.

ENVELOPE (RFC-0036 §"Static CONNECTION, dynamic GRAPH"), stated in the header: reports what has been DISCOVERED and never blocks, so an empty enumeration means "nobody seen yet" and not "nobody exists"; a backend with no graph returns `Unsupported`, which is a different answer from empty.
